findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the upright white cooler closest to the door if the kitchen to measure 50F with the infrared probe. This cooler failure must be a recent occurrence, as the yogurt within the cooler measured 41F with a probe thermometer. All TCS foods within the cooler was transferred to an alternative cold holding unit. PIC was made aware of the failure and plans to contact maintenance. Since the facility has adequate cold holding equipment aside from the cooler that failed, this violation is considered corrected on site with no follow-up needed. Inspector will call occasionally to spot check cooler repair process.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector observed no food handler’s certificates available at the facility. The PIC was informed and has an action plan to certify all kitchen staff. The PIC currently operating the kitchen as a CFPM from previous employment. Ensure all kitchen staff have food handler’s or food manager’s by next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed no certified food manager on duty during food service and preparation. A certified food manager must be on duty at all times that food is being prepared and served. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employee put on new gloves without first washing hands. Discussed proper glove use with employee. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Signed copies of employee health reporting agreements were not available for the GM or any of the staff that work in the breakfast area. Employee health documents were provided and discussed. GM and staff present at the time of inspection signed reporting agreements. Ensure all staff that will work and/or have the potential to help in the breakfast area are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff. 
 The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)
Observed 3 part sink made to have less than than 100ppm of quat sanitizer. The water was 60F. The automatic dispenser mixes sanitizer with cold water below 75F.  The water is so cold that the employees do not like to use it so they add hot water from the sink which decreases the concentration of the the solution. The employees are going to discontinue use of the automatic dispenser and mix sanitizer by hand so that it is at minimum 75F and tests with a test strip to be at least 200ppm. Always follow label directions.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 
Observed the kitchen employee to be drying pans with a cloth towel. The employee was coached and will allow items to air dry form now on.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination. 
Observed the in use box a single use gloves to be stored under the hand soap dispenser at the hand sink. The gloves were removed. Do not store single use gloves where they can become contaminated with splash or soap.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: 4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. Gaskets on the upright refrigerator and Upright freezer doors are in disrepair. Replace the damaged gaskets.
findings.citation_text: 4-202.11 Food-Contact surface at dish drying area is no longer smooth and easily clean able as towels from the hotel have been placed on them. A food-contact surface that is not smooth and easily clean able can harbor bacteria that can be transfered to food. Replace with a National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI approved surface.  Provide drain racks for proper, clean drying area. Towels were removed. Wash dishes and properly drain dry before use.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  
Provide verifiable proof of handler certified employees. Employees who are not certified managers must have certified hander training within 30 days of hire.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Breakfast attendant was observed going between tasks and multiple glove changes without washing hands. In one instance, the attendant was washing dishes and did not wash hands between glove changes before continuing on to food preparation. Handwashing between tasks and glove changes were discussed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands, and prior to putting on gloves.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the handwashing sink in the kitchen. Handwashing signs were provided and posted during inspection.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 In-use tub of whipped butter was observed out on the counter in the kitchen. Internal temperature was observed at 68F-70F. Directions for storage on the lid state to keep refrigerated at 34F-40F. Remaining portion was to be used or discarded by the end of breakfast service. Attendant was advised the whole tub of whipped butter should remain in the cooler and only a small portion removed for use. Any remaining portion must be discarded at the end of breakfast once removed from the original container and held at room temperature during breakfast service. Another tub of whipped butter was also observed out in the storage area. It was still at 39F and was out for ~15 minutes. Whipped butter was placed back in the cooler.    

Cream cheese packets in the bottom of the glass front counter top cooler in the breakfast area had internal temperatures of 46F-47F. Yogurts on the other shelving in the cooler were observed at internal temperatures of 39F-43F depending on location within the cooler. Plastic storage bins are used in the cooler and may be affecting air circulation. GM and attendant were advised to discard leftover portions at the end of breakfast service. GM stated the packets will be placed on another shelf during breakfast tomorrow higher up in the cooler to see if that helps maintain a colder temperature temperature. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Cabinet beneath the coffee maker in the kitchen was soiled with splash. A little splash was on the wall next to the cabinet as well. 
 --A small counter top fryer was observed in the storage area soiled with grease and food debris on the outside. Used oil and food debris were inside the fryer.
Clean the aforementioned items.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Hard cooked eggs in the bottom of the glass front cooler are 48°F when probed. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food (6 eggs) were discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11  (Pf) Food establishment does not have food cooling equipment with adequate capacity for current operations. Provide equipment for cooling food, and holding cold food, that is sufficient in number and capacity to cool food rapidly to required temperatures within the required time frames. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 4-301.11. Eggs were removed and discarded. Provide a proper holding unit for eggs.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14. Sanitizer dispenser used for wiping cloth bucket is not dispensing sanitizer at the proper concentration. Repair this dispenser and use dispenser at 3 part sink until this one is properly repaired.

Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-501.110  (C) Employees were found not using the designated dressing rooms / changing areas or designated employees lockers when changing clothes or storing personal articles. Dressing rooms and lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used if employees regularly change clothes or store personal articles in the establishment while working. Reference 6-501.110.  Observed employee belongings to be on a cart with a hot holding unit in the back room. Store employee belongings seterated from food and food related articles. Jacket was moved.
